title: Two-stage OTA, cascode compensation
description: The Ahuja (cascode) variant of the two-stage Miller OTA: the compensation cap Cc returns to a low-impedance cascode node instead of directly across the second stage. Routing the compensation current through the common-gate cascode blocks the feedforward path, so the right-half-plane zero that plagues plain Miller compensation is removed and the pole-splitting is better damped — for the same GBW the phase margin comes almost entirely from the second pole. The stage structure mirrors the plain Miller OTA (stage-1 input pair + mirror load, stage-2 common source + load); the added cascode device carries the stage-1 branch current and provides the node Cc returns through. The pole and phase-margin rows are ESTIMATE-grade small-signal approximations; the simulator owns stability sign-off. On the demo NMOS table the polarity-inverted devices keep their sign params at +1.

doc.title: Stage-1 mirror-load device
doc.description: One side of the stage-1 mirror load at half the tail current; its diode drop sets the stage-1 output DC and its output conductance loads the first stage.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: Stage-1 input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current; its drain sits at the stage-1 output DC, its source one vgs below the input common mode.

doc.title: Compensation cascode device
doc.description: The common-gate cascode carrying the stage-1 branch current; the compensation cap returns to its low-impedance source, so the feedforward path (and the RHP zero) is blocked.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: Stage-2 common-source device
doc.description: The second-stage gain device carrying the full stage-2 current at the output DC level; its gm sets the second pole and its gate cap dominates the stage-1 output node.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: Stage-2 current-source load
doc.description: The second-stage current-source load carrying the stage-2 current at the output DC level; its output conductance loads the second-stage gain.

rows.name: gm2
rows.note: stage-2 transconductance sets the second pole

rows.name: gm_casc
rows.note: cascode transconductance (sets the impedance of the node Cc returns to)

rows.name: GBW
rows.note: compensated unity-gain bandwidth (input gm into the compensation cap)

rows.name: p2
rows.note: non-dominant pole ESTIMATE; cascode compensation both removes the RHP zero and pushes this pole out — refine C1_est from the stage-2 cgg plus extraction

rows.name: PM
rows.note: ESTIMATE: only the second-pole phase lag remains because the cascode blocks the feedforward RHP zero. Small-signal approximation — the simulator owns stability sign-off

rows.name: SR
rows.note: the smaller slew limit: stage-1 tail charging Cc, or stage-2 current charging CL

rows.name: Av1
rows.note: stage-1 gain into the input-device and mirror-load output conductances

rows.name: Av2
rows.note: stage-2 common-source gain into its own and the load conductances

rows.name: Av
rows.note: two-stage DC gain (product of the stage gains)

rows.name: cgg2
rows.note: stage-2 gate capacitance — the dominant term in the stage-1 output cap C1_est

rules.note: two-stage DC gain meets the target
the worse of the two slew limits meets the target
the compensated bandwidth (gm1/(2*pi*Cc)) meets the target
ESTIMATE-grade phase margin (no RHP zero term); the simulator owns the real stability sign-off
stage-2 device saturated at the output DC level
stage-2 load saturated at the output DC level
the cascode device stays saturated at its node vds
